title: Metrics and Monitoring
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of metrics and monitoring in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to request counts.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers metrics and monitoring within observability and operations. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use metrics and monitoring to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is operational evidence, configuration discipline, failure detection and safe recovery.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Metrics and Monitoring matters because it is part of observability and operations. In practice, focus on operational evidence, configuration discipline, failure detection and safe recovery. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Request counts
items.text: Use request counts as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Latency measurements
items.text: Use latency measurements as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Error rates
items.text: Use error rates to make behavior observable and repeatable. Specify one normal case, one invalid or missing-input case, and the expected status or diagnostic. A passing happy path alone is not enough evidence.

items.title: Resource utilization
items.text: Use resource utilization as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Database and dependency metrics
items.text: Apply database and dependency metrics against a disposable database and synthetic data first. Make transaction ownership and cleanup explicit, parameterize values, and verify constraints and behavior after failures before considering a deployment.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Metrics and Monitoring
content_blocks.run_instructions: Try one existing-style ID and the documented missing-resource case.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Request counts”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Metrics and Monitoring”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Request counts” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Metrics and Monitoring, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Metrics and Monitoring belongs to the broader goal of operational evidence, configuration discipline, failure detection and safe recovery.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
